title: 48 x 48 sprite sheet not showing up correctly in event? (Solved)

posts.author: justloveme94
posts.body: Hello, I was unsure how to search this particular issue and was hoping someone might have the answer. I have a sprite sheet that shows up correctly in tilesets but when I put it in the characters folder to put as the image during an event, the sprite size changes. It is selecting a size larger than 48, cutting off the sprites, and I was wondering how to correct this.

posts.author: strawberryapple
posts.body: What are the dimensions in pixels of the Image [Farming] ?

posts.author: TheAM-Dol
posts.body:
Without the $ sign, the engine will divide the sprite sheet into 12 columns and 8 rows.
(With the sign it will divide the sprite sheet into 3 columns of 4 rows)
It seems like your spritesheet is not formatted correctly.

posts.author: Lady_JJ
posts.body:
It looks like you're using a character sheet and not a tileset. If you're using a tileset, such as [Tileset B] in your listing, then it needs to be 576 pixels by 576 pixels. If you're using a charset, then you need to make it 12 * number of pixels each across and 8 * number of pixels down. (Which is what the others have said.) Look at the Actor1 to see what I mean. 12 images across and 8 images down. So if you're looking to select a 48x48 image, your charset needs to be 576 pixels by 384 pixels.
@Avery
wrote a tutorial explaining the sizes of a charset and when to use a ! and/or a $ and it's well worth reading. You can find it
here.
So, as was asked above, what is the size of the sheet you're using?

If you have sprites that are 48x48, then the sheet needs to be 576 wide by 384 tall. In other words, 12 cells horizontally by 8 cells vertically.

posts.author: TheAM-Dol
posts.body:
justloveme94 said:
The sprite sheet is supposed to be 48 by 48. I tried putting a $ sign in front of the file but it made it bigger.
Click to expand...
That's because you didn't read what I said.
With the $ sign, the sheet is divided into 3 columns and 4 rows.
This makes it a single character sprite sheet with a stepping left, middle, and right (the columns) and the directions down, left, right, up (the rows)
Anyways, glad you got it solved.
